Furthermore, the diversity of equipment provided a refreshing change from other gyms I've visited. From state-of-the-art cardio machines to an extensive range of weights and resistance training equipment, there was something for everyone.  The staff at PureGym Bournemouth were also friendly and helpful, creating a welcoming and supportive environment. They were readily available to assist with any queries or provide guidance on proper exercise techniques.  In conclusion, I highly recommend PureGym Bournemouth to both locals and travelers. THIS REVIEW IS ABOUT PUREGYM GATESHEAD   This gym is good - it has a good variety of machines, its cheapish, the classes are excellent, and the staff are really helpful. The layout is very odd - no mats in the functional area or dumbbells, and the air-conditioning either doesn't work properly or isn't switched on.   The mat area downstairs by the stair machines is so useless - why are there no weights near them? And the hygiene... the spray and hand-towel stations are not spread out enough and there are not enough of them. When downstairs in the 'legs' area I can never find a spray bottle.   But the worst thing for me is that the weight-benches are all crammed into a tiny room off the side which is such a cramped space to work out in, and despite how popular the benches are there are only about 6 in there. In a gym with so many members it is so inadequate.   Such a shame because it could easily be a much better gym. Just needs more hygiene stations,more benches, and a more well thought-out layout. The online sign up process was unclear at times and the student membership discount is somewhat misleading. For instance, it offers the membership at a discount of 30% - but this is only on the most expensive membership available. Therefore, it is actually cheaper to get the (off-peak) membership as they do not offer a corresponding reduction on the cheapest membership. This represents what can only be considered as tactical marketing and/or a seemingly deceptive sales pitch (by silence) when, in reality, the company (Pure Gym) could simply be more upfront. Although they are correct in stating that you get a discount of 30% - it is actually still more expensive (at £19.50 p/m) to get the "discounted" membership. This also includes the burden of a minimum 6 month contract that comes with that "discount" as applied. In reality, it would otherwise be cheaper for potential new members to get a basic off-peak membership at (£15.99) and this comes with the added flexibility of no contract. Above all else, the tactics used here are sneaky and give the impression of value, when it really is not when you view it from a purely financial standpoint.

A very worthwhile modern gym.  Been going to the East Kilbride gym for a few months now and definitely recommend them to people of any skill level.  The staff are very friendly and happy to answer any queries you may have with the machines and if you're as heavily introverted as I am, there's also videos on their website on how to use them and suggested workouts.   The gym has plenty treadmills and cross trainers, and a handful of bikes so plenty of options for cardio. There are plenty dumbbells downstairs but only a handful of weight machines and barbells to use so you may have to wait your turn to use them, especially if its busy (I usually go in the morning so its fairly quiet).  Call me an old man but the music they play is hot garbage. My guess is its a pre-recorded programme of about 50 songs with some ads between songs. Only one of these I find even remotely catchy is a song called Kate's brother (I think). I have heard that batter up swing swing song SO many times I want to claw my eardrums out every time. Fortunately, this is easily rectified by bringing your own headphones.  The gym looks pretty safe despite its location. Entrances are single person vestibules which require a pin (or QR code) granted by your membership to open so no one can tailgate. In addition the place is open 24/7 and while it is not staffed at all hours, Paul, the manager, assures me that there is always someone available to respond to any emergencies if need be.   Docking a few points for the locker room. The (men's) locker room is not in great condition with a number of them not working and not feeling very secure. I'd never leave anything valuable in a locker anyway, but definitely something to be aware of.  Membership I use if £14.99/month this is called the off peak membership which basically means the only time you can't get in is weekday evenings (3.30pm-8:30pm). Any other time is fair game. There's also a joining fee which isn't great, but often they will do promotions where your first month is half price AND there's no joining fee so keep an eye out for these as they are VERY worth it, in my opinion. The higher tier memberships may be better for you if you can't do morning, and/ or you travel a lot or occasionally want to bring a freeloader, I mean, friend along.

Thank you for your feedback regarding the air conditioning in the gym.   We have recently made slight changes to this area, looking at improving energy efficiency. This is both to control our energy usage, but also with a look to reduce our carbon footprint. By law, we have a requirement to provide a certain amount of fresh air based on occupancy levels, and our ventilation system increases and decreases at different times throughout the day and night, making sure we meet these requirements and provide good air movement around the gyms. These levels are based on size of the gym, and occupancy levels, and are regularly monitored.   With regards to the temperature in the gym, we use air conditioning units which heat the air when it drops below 17.5C, and cools the air when it goes higher than 21.5C, keeping the temperature within the gym at an acceptable level. This is regularly checked to ensure the units are operating as they should be across all of our gyms.   On occasion, we can get faults on our ventilation and AC systems which is normal. When this happens, there is a process in place to ensure we arrange for our contractors to attend, investigate and resolve the faults and return the systems back to full working order within a timely manner.   All member feedback is reviewed, and brought to the attention of our Facilities team, who regularly review any changes we make to our gym facilities and all feedback is taken into account when making any future changes.   We hope you continue to enjoy the gym in the meantime!     We'd love to take some feedback on the service provided today. Please click here to complete a 1-minute survey!  Thanks,  Clare   PureGym Member Services

To anyone considering a gym, especially those who might feel intimidated by age or health conditions, PureGym Hammersmith Palais is a wonderful choice. The PureGym branch in East Sheen, London, is a very spacious gym, divided into sections for weight training and cardio. It is well-organized and well-divided. The only problem is that in the weight training area, there is only one flat bench for chest, leading to queues for those wanting to perform their workouts. This is inconceivable for such a large gym, especially considering that bench training is one of the most commonly performed exercises. The same issue applies to the areas designated for squats, with only four zones available. Additionally, two of these zones are often occupied for an extended period by individuals performing deadlifts, (preventing others from using the space for squats) because they have a different flooring. This results in the squat area being occupied.   Simply allocating a few square meters for deadlift flooring, separate from the squat area, would resolve this issue, ensuring better use of space and facilitating a more efficient gym layout.  In summary, the main stations for major muscle groups should be better managed to allow for enjoyable and comfortable workouts without the need to struggle for available space.  I hope that the gym management can takes my suggestions into consideration. I discovered that the cable machines had the wrong stickers on each of the weights so if you thought you were choosing 2.3kg for example it was really 4.3kg. Where the Corner T Bar Row Platform Landmine Attachment Handle is positioned they have placed a carpet by the window / open doors so if it rains the water comes through and makes the carpet extremely wet. Whoever designed the gym left out critical elements. This gym is missing some key machines: Biceps Curl, Triceps press, Lat pulldown, lateral raise, Calf press, Hack squat and there is a very low amount of cardio machines for this price. For example there is only one upright bike.   There is a good amount of Cable machines, but I couldn’t believe they don’t provide a cable straight bar which is the most used attachment for cable machines and a narrow grip landmine handle & row attachment. This is shocking. There is a good amount of functional stuff and that’s about it.   When Puregym opened its doors to the public the first thing I was shocked about was the fact that the changing area, toilets/showers and lockers are all on the same floor and shared between men and women.   There aren’t enough lockers for members and they have also provided open shelves for people to put their possessions in which is ridiculous as there is a sign that says PureGym can’t be held accountable for anything that goes missing. Why didn’t they just provide more lockers?  My frustrations have increased as they opened on the 01/12/2023 and closed 13/12/2023 and didn’t send an email out to members telling us. I found out by going to the gym and seeing a sign saying the place has shut down due to a facilities issue and to use the closest gym to me. When I contacted customer service the only option I was given was to freeze my membership which I would have to pay £6.99 for each month.   I find this preposterous as no emails have been sent out to update members as to when the gym will open again. I could pay £6.99 to freeze my membership and they open tomorrow. We’ve been told to just keep an eye out for an email. This is shocking.  The Gym Group never do this. They give you a timeframe and keep you updated constantly. If I’m made to pay to freeze my membership I’m cancelling my membership. I feel a lot of members will leave after the first six months as the price increase doesn’t reflect the quality of this gym.

We already know we are welcome or people of all races/ ethnicities wouldn't be there!   Then there is the "Strike out Harassment" message. How many reports of Harassment does Pure Gym get on a daily or weekly basis? How many times has someone complained of racism or exclusion from the gym based on race? As a black man that joined Soho Gym in 2004 and been with Pure gym since it took over the site in 2018, I have never experienced any of that.  Meanwhile what I do experience EVERY SINGLE DAY is weights being left by members who are too lazy to replace them after use. I see trip hazards by way of dumbbells and kettle bells and mats being left in the leg press and Hamstring curl training area. I see people leaving loaded barbells on squat racks and have seen ladies who have to unload multiple 20kg plates off the leg press or squat rack left there by some inconsiderate member. (These are then taken off and left on the floor). I see plates leaning up against the weight racks as though lifting them onto the rack was a bridge too far for whoever left it there. All this makes your "Train Safe" message sound like a joke. Repeated behaviour like this does not match your "Train Safe" message, it makes a mockery of it!  Your obligation as a company is to EDUCATE people to show basic levels of gym etiquette and consideration to their fellow members. I even printed off more of your miniscule notices that are hidden from view in corners of the gym. No one takes any notice of those messages so I printed 15 copies to be put in more prominent parts of the gym but was told that head office stated that only 4 posters can be allowed in the gym for fear of "offending" people. I couldn't believe my ears.  At best this policy is a negligent lack of duty of care to your members and at worst it is a policy that displays stupidity of galactic proportions because Pure Gym Head Office prefer to use their email and media resources to remind us black people that we have a history and LGBTQ and non LGBTQ communities that we are all welcome in a place where we already train happily together! BUT you fly 2 Rainbow Flags and 2 large "Everybody Welcome" flags and send us Black History Month emails when you could EASILY use the same resources to EDUCATE the small but determined IGNORANT and INCONSIDERATE members that leave their weights all over the place for your staff and ME to put away. How does that make any sense?  Why not use a flag or banner as big as the current "Everybody Welcome" one to say a simple message "Please replace your weights after use. Repeated failure to do this will result in PIN suspension" Who could possibly get offended by a simple reminder to show basic levels of consideration to their fellow members? We really do live in very strange times! Instead of treating this gym like a creche full of toddlers that may have a tantrum when politely reminded to be considerate, try leaving messages that educate this minority instead of incessantly reminding us of things we already know ("Everybody is Welcome").  I really do hope someone in Head office reads this and uses basic common sense because this is a problem that you really need to address instead of all this "safe place to train" nonsense. A safe and judgement free zone? Give me a break! People ARE being judged for their lazy inconsiderate behavior! Regarding your "safe place to train" nonsense I can assure you I've not been bitten by any snakes or had an attempted kidnapping so yes it is a safe place to train! I mainly joined because of the frequency of spin classes compared to my previous gym (an even lower budget gym in Leeds city centre). However, I would otherwise much prefer to have remained there. I don’t like essentially being in a cave when I work out, without any natural light or phone signal - the fluorescent lights and typical gym smell that hit you as soon as you get in is pretty overwhelming. It also feels quite packed and chaotic when you walk in, and is very much like a fishbowl, with nowhere to hide. Compared to my former gym, there seems to be a much higher percentage of ‘gym bros’ parading around, and I find it quite intimidating that they’re allowed to sit on the bikes behind the instructor on their phones for the whole spin class, not actually participating but watching the rest of us (I was even getting paranoid one was taking photos). The very fact that the spin classes are right in the middle of the gym with everyone watching is in itself daunting. As a whole it feels very impersonal, and the instructors seem great but there just doesn’t seem to be a culture of communicating with each other in classes (possibly due to the transient nature of such gym memberships, with people coming and going). It’s quite nice to be able to slip in and out unnoticed, and I can certainly see the appeal of anonymity when looking and feeling at your absolute worst, but eye contact and a hello/smile/getting to know the names of regulars doesn’t go amiss. I realise a lot of this is down to personal preference, so I don’t expect the gym to be able to do much about this.   However, in terms of improvements, things I would ideally like to see are proactive efforts to make it more inclusive (this worked really well at my former gym - it doesn’t cost much to stick up some posters etc making it clear that people of any shape/size/background are welcome, as well as making women feel safer in what is quite a testosterone-fuelled environment), and practically, a bit of a service of the spin bikes (some of the screens don’t work, foot straps are loose etc) and an improvement on the availability of cleaning products (e.g. spray and paper - the bin never seems to get emptied and they’re always running out). In an ideal world I’d also love to see a bigger variety of classes.

After visiting some of the newer gym locations such as Coleraine and Ballymena I can see that there are a number of improvements that could be made to the Lisburn gym to offer the members better facilities especially in the functional area and weight training areas.   The list of suggestions is as follows: 1. Install a track and sled, with the correct plates to load the sled made available in this area. 2. Install a rack of Blk Box hex dumbbells in the functional area to offer dumbbell weights from 5kg to 22.5kg as is the case with the newer gyms. The current options only go as far as 10kg which is too light for a number of exercises that would be performed in this area. Additionally the Hex shape is much more suited for functional exercises than the circular ended dumbbells that Lisburn currently has. 3. Renovate the weight training area to install a Blk Box rig with weightlifting platforms like there is in the newer gyms. This would increase the number of people who can train at any one time. I acknowledge there is limited space in the venue but I believe that with some reorganisation this could be accommodated given that e.g. Coleraine has all of the suggestions on my list and is working with a much smaller venue. 4. This is linked to point 3 - I suggest adding additional 15kg barbells and replacing/servicing the older barbells that Lisburn currently have. In the newer gyms I've observed that there are usually 3 15kg Belfast bars, and a good number of 20kg Belfast bars and power bars, easily catering for everyone at the gym, whereas Lisburn is quite limited in comparison. Additionally there are not enough 5kg Olympic lifting plates (only 1 pair) which is problematic if someone takes these away from the weight lifting platform. I suggest buying at least 1 new pair of these for the current situation, however if there was to be a rig installed plates would have to be bought in proportion to this. 5. Add 2 concept bikes, to the functional area. I've noticed that Lisburn only has the concept ski erg and rowers, however it would be a welcome addition to be able to have access to concept bikes here too. 6. The flooring in the functional area is spongey making it less stable that the flooring I've experienced elsewhere, and the area itself is quite small. I suggest that the area is refloored with the same material as in the newer gyms and the equipment rearranged to enable this area to cover a larger surface area.  Thanks for taking the time to read my review, and I hope that in time all of the suggestions can be accommodated given this is the standard of equipment and facilities already being offered in the newer gyms.

Inside of the lockers is consistently dirty too and many lockers have the locks left on all week, again not enforced by the staff.   * The rules are not enforced. Multiple laminated  sheets printed out telling people they will be banned for training semi- clothed and not putting their kit back = nothing actually happens.   *Maintenance times. When kit breaks here it takes weeks/ months to fix. Appreciate it’s a big company and Bangor is out in the sticks so to speak, but this is still pretty shoddy. Leg extender machine has had a nice laminated notice on it to not push beyond point 8 for 2 months, but not actually been fixed, shower door as above, cross trainer took 6 weeks + to fix…. When something breaks here there appears to be no sense of urgency from the on site staff particularly or puregym as a company. The urinal in the male changing room was full of Urine for a month not long ago before it was fixed.  * Water. The water as a whole here is an issue and they 100% have an on site issue , I’m a plumber and know what I’m looking for. The water fountain pressure is up and down and barely a dribble, shower pressure ,( when they work), is also barely a dribble and the male urinals flush 24/7, they never stop. This has nothing to do with saving water with regards to the low pressure, this is an on site issue. Again going on for months, again not sorted.   The air con. The pace is stuffy and need good, reliable air circulation. It doesn’t have that, and as a consequence the place is warmer than a gym should be, and the plethora of gym members here who don’t smell every nice make the warm, sticky environment that little bit worse. The place has a smell to it which isn’t pleasant a lot of the time.   Puregym really need to get their act together here, or all they’ll end up with having as members are the students who want a cheap gym membership, and mostly these are the same students who don’t put their weights back/throw their litter away/train half clothed - think on that one for a second.   They also need to employ a management team on site who is more proactive and gets stuff done. The gym and site has gone massively down hill over the last three months and continues to go more down the more time goes on, which will only get worse. The Management team in place at the beginning of the year was more prone to challenging members and keeping on top of kit repairs, rather than laminating a sheet saying they’re doing it and then not actually getting it done. No offence to the current team as they’re lovely people, but they’re meek and reserved and don’t follow up on their promises to get issues sorted. ‘We’ve reported it’ and ‘we’re waiting for an engineer’ only holds so much water. Report more, chase more, until it’s done. That’s customer service, that’s customer satisfaction and that is what this site is missing, which is a shame. As someone who firmly believes in the importance of maintaining physical health and cherishing the concept of a supportive gym environment, it deeply pains me to report that my experience at PureGym has been subpar and largely disappointing.  First and foremost, let's address the primary concern – the staff. One might assume that a gym would hire individuals who are not only knowledgeable about fitness but also understand the importance of maintaining a friendly, approachable, and encouraging environment. Unfortunately, PureGym staff fall short on this. My encounters with the staff have been marred by a conspicuous lack of professionalism and, even worse, a persistent snobbish attitude - especially from Klaudia and Mariana.  Instead of fostering an atmosphere of motivation, empathy, and camaraderie, interactions with the staff members at PureGym felt more like a chore. More than once, they displayed an unhelpful, dismissive, and condescending demeanor, especially towards new members. They showed a disturbingly evident lack of patience and, to be blunt, their overall behavior could be best described as unwelcoming.  Working out, especially for beginners, can be a challenging endeavor. It requires motivation, support, and above all, a non-judgmental space. Sadly, PureGym seemed to have forgotten this crucial component of its business model. It felt as though there was an unwritten hierarchy at play, with the staff favoring the more 'accomplished' gym-goers, leaving beginners and intermediates feeling alienated and ignored.  The lack of professional conduct is not just limited to interactions. Their disinterest also manifests in the upkeep of the gym itself. Cleanliness and hygiene, which should be of utmost importance in such spaces, have been overlooked, leading to an unsanitary and off-putting environment. The locker rooms were often in a disarray, the showers were not clean, and used towels were frequently left unattended.  Moreover, the equipment's maintenance leaves much to be desired. Several machines were either in a state of disrepair or showed signs of wear and tear. Although these issues were reported to the staff, there seemed to be a glaring lack of urgency or even interest in resolving them.  In the realm of fitness, where progress hinges on consistency, motivation, and a supportive environment, the culture at PureGym was counterproductive. There seemed to be an exclusive, unwelcoming 'clique culture' perpetuated by the staff that overshadowed any positives the gym might have had.  Overall, my experience at PureGym has been unsatisfactory. Their inattentiveness towards the members' needs, failure to maintain a clean and well-kept facility, and the general air of snobbishness significantly detracted from the gym's potential. At a time when physical and mental health is being given so much importance globally, it is a shame to see such a stark deviation from the supportive, encouraging environment one would expect from a gym. I hope PureGym takes these concerns seriously and commits to providing a better service in the future. Until such improvements are made, I find it difficult to recommend this gym to others.

I recently reactivated my membership with the off-peak package at Pure Gym Enfield, enticed by its affordable price of £22. However, my experience has been far from satisfactory.  The main issue with the off-peak package is that it restricts users to access the gym only after 21:00. This limitation has resulted in overcrowding during the available hours, making it incredibly challenging to find any space, machines, or free weights to use. It defeats the purpose of a gym membership if you cannot utilise the facilities due to excessive demand.  Pure Gym Enfield offers a solution to this problem by providing an upgrade option for an additional £7, allowing subscribers to access the facilities at any time. However, this feels like an unnecessary expense to overcome the gym's own overcrowding issue.  Furthermore, I found the standards at the gym to be disappointing. The ventilation system appears to be inadequate, especially when the air conditioning is not in operation. Poor ventilation poses a potential health and safety risk, particularly during intense workout sessions when fresh airflow is crucial.  Overall, my experience at Pure Gym Enfield has been unsatisfactory. The overcrowding issue during off-peak hours, coupled with the need to pay extra for a better workout experience, has left me disappointed. The subpar ventilation system further exacerbates the problems and raises concerns about the gym's commitment to its members' well-being.  I hope that Pure Gym Enfield takes these issues into consideration and makes the necessary improvements to provide a better experience for its members.

I recently joined the new gym in town and wanted to share my experience. Overall, I am thoroughly impressed with the facility and the top-notch equipment they provide. However, there is one major drawback that I must mention—the limited availability due to its popularity.  Let's start with the positives. The gym boasts an extensive range of state-of-the-art exercise equipment. From cardio machines to free weights and resistance training, they have everything you need for a comprehensive workout. The equipment is well-maintained, and you can tell that the gym management takes pride in providing a high-quality fitness experience.  The gym itself is spacious, clean, and well-designed. It creates an inviting atmosphere that motivates you to push your limits and achieve your fitness goals. The staff members are friendly, knowledgeable, and always ready to assist you if needed. The cleanliness of the facility is commendable, with staff regularly sanitizing equipment and maintaining a hygienic environment.  Now, let's address the issue of limited availability. Due to the gym's popularity and the sheer number of members, finding an open spot during peak hours can be quite challenging. The gym gets very busy, and sometimes it feels overcrowded, especially during evenings and weekends. This can be a bit frustrating, as it may lead to longer wait times for machines or difficulty accessing certain areas of the gym.  To their credit, the gym management is aware of this problem and actively working on solutions. They have introduced online booking systems and are considering expanding their facilities to accommodate more members. However, it will take some time before these measures fully alleviate the issue. In the meantime, it would be wise to plan your visits during off-peak hours if possible.  Despite the availability issue, I would still highly recommend this gym for its exceptional equipment and overall quality. If you can manage to adjust your workout schedule or don't mind occasional waits, the benefits of training at this gym outweigh the inconvenience. Just be prepared for the busy periods and plan your workouts accordingly.  In conclusion, this gym offers a fantastic fitness experience with top-notch equipment and a well-maintained facility. However, the limited availability due to high demand can be a challenge during peak hours. If you're willing to work around that, you'll find a gym that provides an excellent environment for achieving your fitness goals.

Some days, it’s like walking into a sauna. It’s often humid, smells sweaty and is too warm to be able to train effectively. This isn’t usually on very hot days. Yesterday (30/06/23) was so bad, I didn’t train and left after speaking to the manager. I have asthma and started to feel breathless after just a few minutes inside the gym. (My asthma is well-regulated and I always check my Sp02 before and after entering the gym.) My peak flow was fine but the stuffy air made me feel faint quite quickly.)  I’ve spoken to the manager on various occasions about the inconsistency of the gym’s air quality and temperature, and he has told me that the air-con is set to a minimum of 20 degrees. This is warm for a gym and especially uncomfortable for high intensity cardio exercise. He told me that he CAN’T change the temperature. Pure Gym has stated on Twitter that individual gym managers control their gym’s temperature and ventilation system; there is no company policy that dictates it.  According to Conor the manager,  this is the temperature that keeps the bills down and most people don’t complain because they don’t do cardio. He can’t change it because he won’t change it, is his explanation in a nutshell.  I’m a PT (and also Exercise Referral qualified) so am well aware of the impact on physical performance as temperature progresses. For people who want to run, row, cycle etc, it’s really uncomfortable and can cause faintness, with the potential for injury.  I’m pretty close to cancelling my membership at this point, having tried unsuccessfully to deal with this directly.  Update  Gym temperature  04/07/23: 22 degrees

We went for the first time this evening (opening day). Was a fantastic experience, really well laid out with changing rooms/toilet facilities on the second floor (they also have a lift). The equipment I used had explanations on how to use and each piece of equipment is colour coded in regards to which area of the body it is used to work. The equipment is all in the same area for each body part (eg all the equipment used to work your arms is in the same area). Good selection in the vending machines. Really clean changing area/locker area with hairdryers and a machine (costs £1) to measure your weight, height, BMI etc. Showers are decent too. Staff are incredibly friendly and always available to help if/when needed. Although we walked there is also free parking for a certain length of time. There is a Poundland next door too.  Only issues were there is only one cubicle for changing after using the shower and lockers were on the smaller side, however the pros definitely outweigh the cons!
